channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average shrugs off hot PPI and an island shopping list
item.description: After Wednesday's near 2% drubbing, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) spent Thursday doing something stranger than falling: very little.

item.title: Japanese Yen struggles near 160.50 as intervention fears offset US Dollar strength
item.description: USD/JPY struggles for direction on Thursday as fears of intervention by Japanese authorities cap upside, even as the US Dollar (USD) strengthens amid renewed hostilities between the United States and Iran.

item.title: Australian Dollar falls to two-month low after hot US PPI and steady jobless claims
item.description: The AUD/USD pair trades near the 0.6980 level on Thursday, hovering near a two-month low as the Australian Dollar (AUD) remains pressured by cautious market sentiment and renewed US Dollar (USD) demand. At the time of writing, the pair trades at 0.6994, down 0.15% on the day.

item.title: China: Export prices still damp global inflation – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered economists Hunter Chan and Shuang Ding argue that higher Oil and AI-related goods prices have lifted China’s import prices and PPI, ending a multi-year deflation spell.

item.title: British Pound slips as war-driven PPI fuels US Dollar rebound
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) registers losses of 0.19% on Thursday after the latest US inflation report reflected the impact of the Iran war on producer prices, while an escalation of hostilities between Washington and Tehran triggered a recovery in Oil prices.

item.title: LatAm FX: Carry resilience versus Fed repricing – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu says Latin American currencies remain relatively resilient even as iFlow data show declining positions in high-yielders under a new Federal Reserve backdrop.

item.title: Bank of Japan: Gradual normalisation with higher JGB yields – ING
item.description: ING’s Min Joo Kang expects the Bank of Japan to deliver a 25bp rate hike in June, supported by resilient growth, negative real rates and upside inflation risks. Despite soft May inflation, underlying pressures and firm wages justify further normalisation.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Downside risk against US Dollar as BoC stays patient – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports the Bank of Canada (BoC) kept its policy rate at 2.25% for a fifth consecutive meeting and signaled no urgency to hike despite two-way optionality.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Pressure persists toward 162 against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report USD/JPY is steady but elevated, with recent gains already surpassing prior intervention-trigger levels. A 25 bps Bank of Japan (BoJ) hike on Tuesday is widely anticipated, and markets price nearly one more increase by December.

item.title: Swiss National Bank: Policy pause and FX stance – Nomura
item.description: Nomura analysts Josie Anderson, George Buckley, Andrzej Szczepaniak and David Seif expect the SNB to keep its policy rate at 0.00% at the 18 June meeting. They highlight low Swiss inflation, mixed activity data and ongoing Iran war uncertainty.

item.title: Gold hits six-month low as hawkish Fed bets, stronger US Dollar weigh
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) slides to a six-month low on Thursday, wiping out all the gains recorded this year as a combination of hawkish central bank expectations, a stronger US Dollar (USD) and technical selling keeps buyers on the sidelines.

item.title: Bank of England: One summer hike seen as likely – ING
item.description: ING’s James Smith highlights a softer UK backdrop than in 2022, with vacancies falling, unemployment rising and wage growth slowing, while firms and workers have limited pricing and bargaining power. He judges that the Bank of England (BoE) is torn between a prolonged pause and a symbolic move.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Overbought US Dollar eyes 1.40–1.41 range – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight renewed Canadian Dollar (CAD) weakness as softer Oil prices and geopolitical concerns push USD/CAD to new year-to-date highs.

item.title: Euro fails to gain traction as geopolitical risks overshadow ECB rate hike
item.description: EUR/USD struggles near two-month lows on Thursday as traders show a muted reaction to the latest European Central Bank (ECB) interest rate decision. Meanwhile, escalating tensions in the Middle East keep risk sentiment subdued and support the US Dollar (USD), leaving the Euro (EUR) on the defensive.

item.title: European Central Bank: Further tightening path outlined – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Jan von Gerich and Tuuli Koivu note that the European Central Bank (ECB) raised rates by 25bp and signalled readiness to tighten further as inflation stays above target.

item.title: Oil: Supply fears and $150 risk flagged – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage highlights that Oil initially spiked on renewed U.S.–Iran tensions before easing, but analysts remain concerned about supply risks and the durability of any peace deal.

item.title: ECB Press Conference: Lagarde speaks on policy outlook after raising rates in June
item.description: Christine Lagarde, President of the European Central Bank (ECB), explains the ECB's decision to raise key rates by 25 basis points at the June policy meeting and responds to questions from the press.

item.title: Lagarde speech: Short-term inflation expectations have risen
item.description: Christine Lagarde, President of the European Central Bank (ECB), explains the ECB's decision to raise key rates by 25 basis points at the June policy meeting and responds to questions from the press.

item.title: United Kingdom: Upside CPI risks building into 2027 – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Sanjay Raja expects UK headline CPI to edge up to 3.01% year-on-year in May, with core CPI at 2.72% and Services CPI at 3.65%. The bank projects CPI to average 3.1% this year before easing to 2.6% next year and 2.3% in 2028, with risks to inflation seen skewed to the upside.

item.title: “There will be more bombing tonight”: US President Trump declares
item.description: United States (US) President Donald Trump said on Thursday that negotiations with Iran remain ongoing but warned of further military action, stating that additional strikes are expected later in the day. Trump made these statements in a Fox News interview.

item.title: Reserve Bank of Australia: Output gap signals prolonged hold – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Prashant Newnaha and Howard Du argue recent weak Australian data and Federal Budget tax changes should keep the RBA cash rate at 4.35% next week and likely on hold for longer.

item.title: Lagarde speech: We did not discuss alternatives
item.description: Christine Lagarde, President of the European Central Bank (ECB), explains the ECB's decision to raise key rates by 25 basis points at the June policy meeting and responds to questions from the press.

item.title: Silver price hits multi‑month low as Fed hike expectations, safe-haven demand weigh
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) extends its bearish move on Thursday and trades around $63.00, down 0.58% on the day at the time of writing.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Growth outlook steady with soft GDP – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economist Claire Fan notes that Canada’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) contracted in Q1, but measures of excess slack such as the unemployment rate still align with prior tracking. Fan keeps its growth outlook unchanged, instead lowering potential GDP estimates.

item.title: Lagarde speech: Conflict is weighing on activity
item.description: Christine Lagarde, President of the European Central Bank (ECB), explains the ECB's decision to raise key rates by 25 basis points at the June policy meeting and responds to questions from the press.

item.title: Oil: Chinese demand and US exports shape balance – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson notes that weaker Chinese crude imports and strong US exports have temporarily eased pressure on Oil, but he stresses these supports are not sustainable. China’s May 2026 crude imports fell sharply, while higher US exports are being drawn from inventories.

item.title: Swiss Franc: FX intervention focus – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s European economics team expects the SNB to keep emphasising an elevated willingness to intervene in FX markets, despite recent CHF depreciation against EUR.

item.title: United States producer inflation jumps to 6.5% in May, highest since November 2022
item.description: Producer inflation in the United States (US) as measured by the change in the Producer Price Index (PPI), climbed to its highest level since November 2022 at 6.5% in May, from 5.7% in April, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Thursday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Limited impact from BoJ leadership absence – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes USD/JPY is trading tightly around 160.50, just below its late-April pre-intervention high, with a 25 bps Bank of Japan (BoJ) rate hike to 1.00% already fully priced.

item.title: US President Trump: Will be hitting Iran very hard tonight
